title: Chocolate Brownies
subtitle: Dense, fudgy chocolate brownies with a crackled top
excerpt: Rich dark chocolate and butter brownies with a glossy, crackled top and a dense, fudgy centre. Baked just until the edges are set and the middle still wobbles slightly in the tin.

recipe.sourceNotes: The brownie was created in the United States in the 1890s and became one of the defining American baked goods of the twentieth century. The word 'brownie' is American in origin; British bakers adopted it via American cookbooks and it became popular in Britain from the 1980s onwards. There are two schools of brownie: cakey, which contains baking powder and produces a lighter, more springy result, and fudgy, which contains no leavening and produces a dense, intensely chocolatey square. The fudgy version is more popular and more technically demanding: the difference between underdone and perfectly set is a matter of minutes in the oven. The crackled top is created by the sugar dissolving in the eggs and forming a thin, glossy crust as it bakes.

recipeTools.notes: A 20 x 30 cm brownie tin or shallow roasting tin, lined with baking parchment.

content.text: The brownie is done when the edges are set and beginning to pull from the sides of the tin but the centre still has a slight wobble when you shake the tin. It will firm up as it cools. Overbaking produces a drier, cakier result. Cool completely in the tin before cutting: the brownies will be too soft and crumbly to cut neatly when warm. Use the best dark chocolate you can find; at least 70 per cent cocoa solids.

items.preparation: 70 per cent cocoa, broken into pieces

content.text: Heat the oven to 180 C / fan 160 C / gas 4. Grease and line a 20 x 30 cm brownie tin. Melt the chocolate and butter together in a bowl over simmering water (or in the microwave in 30-second bursts). Stir until smooth. Cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk the sugar, eggs, and vanilla together in a large bowl for 3 minutes until thickened and pale. Stir in the warm chocolate mixture.

Sift in the flour, cocoa, and salt. Fold until just combined with no flour streaks. Pour into the tin and bake for 22 to 26 minutes until the edges are set but the centre still wobbles slightly. Cool completely in the tin. Cut into 16 squares.
